Rather than the generic statewide statements, the Town should consider providing explicit factual findings from the Town supporting the moratorium, such as: "The Town Board hereby finds and determines that: 1. The Town has recently received inquiries or development pressures related to nuclear energy generation technologies and large-scale data storage facilities. 2. These uses present significant concerns related to electrical grid capacity, high-volume water consumption, noise generation, emergency services capability, and long-term environmental impact. 3. The Town's existing Zoning Law does not contain adequate standards or districts to properly regulate such high-intensity uses. 4. Absent a temporary moratorium, applications may proceed in a manner inconsistent with sound planning principles, thereby creating risks of haphazard development and irreversible impacts on community character. PLANNING BOARD Crossroads Center NYS Route 19 Belmont, NY 14813 585-268-7472 www.alleganyco.gov E-Mail: kier.dirlam@alleganyco.gov October 21, 2026 D) Town of New Hudson – Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers LOCAL LAW OF 2026 TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON DATA CENTERS BE IT ENACTED BY THE TOWN BOARD OF THE TOWN OF NEW HUDSON AS FOLLOWS: Section 1. Title. This Local Law shall be known as the "Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers within the Town of New Hudson". Section 2. Purpose. Pursuant to the statutory powers vested in the Town Board of the Town of New Hudson to protect the health, safety and welfare of its residents, the Town Board hereby declares a one-year moratorium on applications, construction, use and placement of Data Centers in the Town. Among the concerns are the large consumption of electricity by these facilities and potential impact of these demands on the cost of energy for residents and the current energy infrastructure. Title. This Local Law shall be known as the "Temporary Moratorium on Battery Energy Storage Systems within the Town of New Hudson". Section 2. Purpose. Pursuant to the statutory powers vested in the Town Board of the Town of New Hudson to protect the health, safety and welfare of its residents, the Town Board hereby declares a one-year moratorium on applications, construction, use and placement of Battery Energy Storage Systems ("BESS") in the Town. The Town Board finds that the New York State Energy Research and Development Authority ("NYSERDA") has advised municipalities to develop comprehensive regulations for a BESS with an aggregate energy capacity greater than 600kWh. This moratorium does not apply to a BESS with an aggregate energy capacity less than or equal to 600kWh that is a single energy storage system for a single-family home or local business. The Town Board is also aware that the Town does not adequately address laws for firefighting, safety, decommissioning and other reported concerns related with large capacity BESS. The Town Board finds that a moratorium of one year is a sufficient time period to draft appropriate regulations. Based on these concerns, the Town Board finds that the
